question: In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1896, the standing corps of the European Border and Coast Guard is to reach a target capacity of 10 000 staff by 2027, comprising 3 000 officers employed directly by Frontex and 7 000 officers seconded by Member States. At the same time, Frontex reported 2 545 occupied posts at the end of 2024 and in June 2026 some 3 800 officers stationed at the EU’s external borders. In light of the above: 1.

What is the current numerical breakdown of Frontex staff between standing corps officers who are actually deployed on operational activities, officers undergoing training or on standby, and staff carrying out administrative, analytical, training, logistical and fundamental rights monitoring tasks?

In which Member States, Schengen associated countries and third countries are standing corps officers currently deployed, how many officers perform tasks directly related to border protection and how many to return activities?

How does the Commission intend to ensure that the further increase in Frontex staff to 10 000 will translate first and foremost into a more effective presence of officers at the EU’s external borders and more effective returns, rather than an expansion of the Agency’s administration?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.8.2026) As sub-questions one and two fall under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide a response to the questions raised by the Honourable Member. The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.

The European Border and Coast Guard standing corps of 10 000 consist of statutory staff employed by Frontex (category 1), operational staff seconded by Member States for long-term deployments (category 2) and operational staff made available by Member States for shortterm deployments.

The standing corps, including the Agency’s statutory staff, is expected to carry out operational tasks primarily as members of the teams in line with the Agency’s core activities. The Commission, as a member of the Management Board, monitors the Agency’s regular reporting on both operational and administrative staff.
